simple.meaning: מָלַךְ (mâlak) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to reign ; inceptively, to ascend the throne ; causatively, to induct into royalty; hence (by implication) to take counsel.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 351 times across Genesis, Exodus, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, and 2 more, beginning at Genesis 36:31. Its contexts include family line, death, kingship, city, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָלַךְ (H4427).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מָלַךְ (mâlak) / H4427 is traced through Genesis 36:31, Genesis 36:32, Genesis 36:33, Genesis 36:34 as a generated source-based concept entry.

majorEvents.evidenceText: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build Yahweh’s house.

majorEvents.evidenceText: He gathered men to himself, and became captain over a troop, when David killed them of Zobah. They went to Damascus, and lived there, and reigned in Damascus.

majorEvents.label: Movement or place
majorEvents.evidenceText: Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in his father David’s city; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

majorEvents.label: Movement or place
majorEvents.evidenceText: Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which Yahweh had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
